The measure appears to be a cross-country poverty indicator expressed as a percentage of population, using international-$ at 2021 prices.
The chart covers countries worldwide, but some places are marked as having no data.

The footnote says the measure may refer to either income after taxes and benefits or to consumption per capita, depending on the country and year.
Since the legend runs from 0% to 100%, darker shading corresponds to a larger share of the population below the threshold.
Several countries or territories appear to have no data, which limits complete global comparison.
